verses.commentary:
42:1-6 This is Job's second
response to YHWH's questioning. It produces a verbal and spiritual
response from Job, as the first speeches of YHWH (Job 38:1-40:2) did
not. This second speech of YHWH (Job 40:6-41:34) obviously had an affect
on Job.

verses.zh: 我知道，你万事都能做；你的旨意不能拦阻。
verses.en: “I know that you can do all things;no purpose of yours can be thwarted;
verses.commentary:
42:2 This verse is an affirmation
of YHWH's sovereignty, power, and purpose.

- He can do all things.

- His purpose(s) cannot be thwarted (i.e., Jer. 23:20; Lam. 2:17; Zech. 1:6).

Number 2 is an affirmation that YHWH has a "plan" for His world.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "know" This
VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT) is
used often in Job. In Job 42, it is used in 42:2,3,11. It has several connotations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

verses.zh: 谁用无知的言语使你的旨意隐藏呢？我所说的是我不明白的；这些事太奇妙，是我不知道的。
verses.en: you asked,[NOTE:1] ‘Who is this who darkens counsel without knowledge?’But[NOTE:2] I have declared without understanding[NOTE:3] things too wonderful for me to know.[NOTE:4]
notes: The expression “you asked” is added here to clarify the presence of the line to follow. Many commentators delete it as a gloss from Job 38:2. If it is retained, then Job has to be recalling God’s question before he answers it.
The word לָכֵן (lakhen) is simply “but,” as in Job 31:37.
Heb “and I do not understand.” The expression serves here in an adverbial capacity. It also could be subordinated as a complement: “I have declared [things that] I do not understand.”
The last clause is “and I do not know.” This is also subordinated to become a dependent clause.
verses.commentary:
42:3 Job repeats God's
characterization of him from Job 38:2. See notes there.

Job clearly admits his presumption in attacking God's character and
justice. He spoke out of limited knowledge and personal pain. His
wonderful faith (i.e., Job 1-2) and blamelessness was evident but his
knowledge of God and His ways was limited. If Job is from Edom and if he
lived during the Patriarchal Period, he did not have the inspired
revelation given to Moses. It is uncertain where his knowledge of the
one true God came from. I personally think a later Judean court sage
took the story of a historical Job and used it to express his own theology
informed by Moses and Wisdom Literature.

▣ "too wonderful for me"
See
SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

verses.zh: 求你听我，我要说话；我问你，求你指示我。
verses.en: You said,[NOTE:1] ‘Pay attention, and I will speak;I will question you, and you will answer me.’
notes: This phrase, “you said,” is supplied in the translation to introduce the recollection of God’s words.
verses.commentary:
42:4 Job uses two IMPERATIVES as requests to YHWH.

- hear – BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE

- instruct – BDB 393, KB 390, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

Job recognizes he needs more information about YHWH. He is now ready to
hear. This is the exact opposite of Job 38:3, where it is stated (in
YHWH's words) that initially Job wanted to question God.

Job 42:4 seems to be a reference to YHWH's words in Job 38:3; 40:7.

verses.zh: 我从前风闻有你，现在亲眼看见你。
verses.en: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear,but now my eye has seen you.[NOTE:1]
notes: This statement does not imply there was a vision. He is simply saying that this experience of God was real and personal. In the past his knowledge of God was what he had heard—hearsay. This was real.
verses.commentary:
42:5 One wonders what this verse is intending to assert.

- Job did not "know" God before

- Job had not personally visited with God (theophany) before

Obviously, Job had a powerful, personal, faith relationship with YHWH
(i.e., Job 1-2). However, how he knew Him and how much he knew
about Him is uncertain.

- ANE general revelation (Ps. 19:1-6; Romans 1-2)

- some contact with YHWH's covenant people

- oral traditions of the Patriarchs

This same question could be asked of Melchizedek, King of Salem (Gen.
14:17-24); Jethro, Moses' father-in-law (Exodus 2); Balaam (Numbers 22);
or the Ninevites of Jonah's day.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

▣ "But now my eyes see You"
Job has been wanting to meet with God. This phrase may be seen to refer
to Job 19:24-27. Job's faith-desire has been met! His greatest pain had
been that God had become his enemy (cf. Job 13:24; 33:10)! Not so now!

verses.zh: 因此我厌恶自己（或译：我的言语），在尘土和炉灰中懊悔。
verses.en: Therefore I despise myself,[NOTE:1] and I repent in dust and ashes!”
notes: Or “despise what I said.” There is no object on the verb; Job could be despising himself or the things he said (see L. J. Kuyper, “Repentance of Job,” VT 9 [1959]: 91-94).
verses.commentary:
42:6

NASB
"I retract"

NKJV
"I abhor myself"

NRSV
"I despise myself"

TEV
"I am ashamed of all I have said"

NJB
"I retract what I have said"

JPSOA
"I recant"

REB
"I yield"

LXX
"I disparaged myself"

Peshitta
"I will keep silent"

The MT has the VERB (BDB
549, KB 540, Qal IMPERFECT,
with no OBJECT), which can mean

- reject, refuse

- despise

- withdraw (UBS Text Project, p. 162)

- melt (NEB, an emendation)

Several translations have tried to supply an
OBJECT

- myself – NKJV, NRSV, LXX

- what he had said – TEV, NJB

The UBS Text Project gives #1,2 a "C" rating (considerable
doubt). It suggests two translations.

- I am overwhelmed

- I withdraw (charges)

I like #2 best in this context.

▣ "I repent" This
is parallel to "I retract" (see notes above). This is not the
most common VERB for
repentance (BDB 996, KB 1427), but it (BDB 636, KB 688, Niphal
PERFECT with waw)
is used often for the deep emotion felt by humans in rebellion against
God (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE [OT]).

In light of the rest of the book of Job, Job admits all humans sin (cf.
Job 5:7). Job admits he is not sinless (cf. Job 6:2-3; 7:20-21; 12:4;
13:23; 14:17; 19:4), but he asserts again and again that he did
not sin in such a way as to bring the terrible punishment that he has
experienced (cf. Job 6:10; 7:20; 9:20-21; 10:6-7,14; 27:1-6; 29:11-20;
32:1; 33:8-12; 34:5). Therefore, this must refer, not to his admittance
of sin, but to his arrogant statements against God. Job wanted his day
in court (cf. Job 9:32; 13:2,3; 14:13; 24:1; 31:35-37), now he sees how
wrong-headed this approach was. The problem was his attitude and limited
knowledge.

▣ "in dust and ashes"
This could be

- the place Job was sitting (cf. Job 2:8)

- an idiom for the grieving rites of the ANE (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES)

verses.zh: 耶和华对约伯说话以后，就对提幔人以利法说：「我的怒气向你和你两个朋友发作，因为你们议论我不如我的仆人约伯说的是。
verses.en: After the Lord had spoken these things to Job, he[NOTE:1] said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My anger is stirred up[NOTE:2] against you and your two friends because you have not spoken about me what is right,[NOTE:3] as my servant Job has.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” The title has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “is kindled.”

The form נְכוֹנָה (nekhonah) is from כּוּן (kun, “to be firm; to be fixed; to be established”). Here it means “the right thing” or “truth.” The Akkadian cognate kīnu means “true, just, honest, firm” (CAD K: 389).
verses.commentary:
42:7-9 This strophe (returns to
prose, like Job 1-2) is YHWH's response to Job's three comforters. I
must confess that I am surprised by YHWH's rejection of them. Their
theology was no less informed than Job's. Their attitudes were no more
wrong than Job's. Job 42:7 is a strong rejection.

- My wrath (BDB 60 I) is kindled against you all

- you have not spoken of Me what is right (i.e., Job 13:8)

Notice the divine affirmation of Job (cf. Job 42:8)

- called "My servant" (i.e., honorific title used four
times in two verses; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT)

- what he spoke about God is "right" (BDB 465 I, KB 464, Niphal
PARTICIPLE), which means "be established"
or "steadfast" or "properly affixed"

This is so surprising! How has Job been "right"; not in his
unfair statements about God or his bad attitudes. It must refer to his
steadfast trust and faith in God.

42:7 This is a typical
Patriarchal idiom (cf. Gen. 25:8; 35:29; 1 Chr. 29:28).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the purpose of the Book of Job in the canon?

- Did God ever explain to Job the reason for his personal suffering? Why or why not?

- What is Satan's place in the scheme?

- Why is Elihu not mentioned in the last chapter?

- How is God's answer to Job also significant to us?

verses.zh: 现在你们要取七只公牛，七只公羊，到我仆人约伯那里去，为自己献上燔祭，我的仆人约伯就为你们祈祷。我因悦纳他，就不按你们的愚妄办你们。你们议论我，不如我的仆人约伯说的是。」
verses.en: So now take[NOTE:1] seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. And my servant Job will intercede[NOTE:2] for you, and I will respect him,[NOTE:3] so that I do not deal with you[NOTE:4] according to your folly,[NOTE:5] because you have not spoken about me what is right, as my servant Job has.”[NOTE:6]
notes: The imperatives in this verse are plural, so all three had to do this together.
The verb “pray” is the Hitpael from the root פָּלַל (palal). That root has the main idea of arbitration; so in this stem it means “to seek arbitration [for oneself],” or “to pray,” or “to intercede.”
Heb “I will lift up his face,” meaning, “I will regard him.”
This clause is a result clause, using the negated infinitive construct.
The word “folly” can also be taken in the sense of “disgrace.” If the latter is chosen, the word serves as the direct object. If the former, then it is an adverbial accusative.

The difference between what they said and what Job said, therefore, has to do with truth. Job was honest, spoke the truth, poured out his complaints, but never blasphemed God. For his words God said he told the truth. He did so with incomplete understanding, and with all the impatience and frustration one might expect. Now the friends, however, did not tell what was right about God. They were not honest; rather, they were self-righteous and condescending. They were saying what they thought should be said, but it was wrong.
verses.commentary:
42:8 God tells the three what
they must do to be restored to right standing.

- take blood offerings – BDB 542, KB 534, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL

- go to Job – BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL

- offer up a burnt offering (burnt sacrifices predate Moses, cf. Gen. 8:20-21; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: SACRIFICES IN MESOPOTAMIA AND ISRAEL AND THEIR SIGNIFICANCE)

- ask Job to pray for them

▣ "seven" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE.

▣

NASB, NKJV
"accept him"

NRSV
"I will accept his prayers"

TEV
"I will answer his prayer"

NJB, REB
"I shall show him favour"

JPSOA
"I will show favor"

Peshitta
"I will accept"

The MT has "for his face I will lift up," which is a legal
idiom for acceptance by a judge at the end of litigation. It is used
several times in Job (i.e., at the beginning of litigation, cf. Job
13:8; 32:21; 34:19).

▣ "folly" This
NOUN (BDB 615) is often
used of disregard for moral guidelines, but that sense does not fit
here. The KB (664 II) suggests "insulting behavior."

For a full discussion of the semantic field of this word see NIDOTTE,
vol. 3, pp. 11-13.

verses.zh: 于是提幔人以利法、书亚人比勒达、拿玛人琐法照着耶和华所吩咐的去行；耶和华就悦纳约伯。
verses.en: So they went, Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite, and did just as the Lord had told them; and the Lord had respect for Job.[NOTE:1]
notes: The expression “had respect for Job” means God answered his prayer.
verses.commentary:
42:9 When the three comforters
were obedient, it does not say YHWH "accepted" them but that
He "accepted" Job! Here is Job's judicial (i.e., "lift
the face") declaration of innocence. His reputation is restored
(and soon all else will be also, Job 42:10-17).

Surprisingly, it is never stated that his physical problems are
healed/resolved. This is assumed because fellowship with his family,
friends, and community is again possible (cf. Job 42:11).

verses.zh: 约伯为他的朋友祈祷。耶和华就使约伯从苦境（原文是掳掠）转回，并且耶和华赐给他的比他从前所有的加倍。
verses.en: So the Lord[NOTE:1] restored what Job had lost[NOTE:2] after he prayed for his friends,[NOTE:3] and the Lord doubled[NOTE:4] all that had belonged to Job.
notes: The paragraph begins with the disjunctive vav, “Now as for the Lord, he….”

The expression here is interesting: “he returned the captivity of Job,” a clause used elsewhere in the Bible of Israel (see e.g., Ps 126). Here it must mean “the fortunes of Job,” i.e., what he had lost. There is a good deal of literature on this; for example, see R. Borger, “Zu šub šb(ī)t,” ZAW 25 (1954): 315-16; and E. Baumann, ZAW 6 (1929): 17ff.

This is a temporal clause, using the infinitive construct with the subject genitive suffix. By this it seems that this act of Job was also something of a prerequisite for restoration—to pray for them.
The construction uses the verb “and he added” with the word “repeat” (or “twice”).
verses.commentary:
42:10-17 This describes the
restoration of Job's possessions, as Job 42:9 described the restoration
of his reputation. Job had never asked for this. He was more concerned
about his good name (Job 42:11).

42:10 "The Lord restored" This
VERB (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal
PERFECT) is the common
root for "repentance" (lit. "to turn back"). Job
"repents" in Job 42:6, now YHWH reciprocates (i.e., different
root, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT); also see NIDOTTE,
vol. 4, p. 58). YHWH "restores" (i.e., "restores the
fortunes of") Job. Often this word is translated "return from
captivity," but here and Jer. 30:3, it denotes restoration of a
previous condition.

verses.zh: 约伯的弟兄、姊妹，和以先所认识的人都来见他，在他家里一同吃饭；又论到耶和华所降与他的一切灾祸，都为他悲伤安慰他。每人也送他一块银子和一个金环。
verses.en: So they came to him, all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before, and they dined[NOTE:1] with him in his house. They comforted him and consoled him for all the trouble the Lord had brought on him, and each one gave him a piece of silver[NOTE:2] and a gold ring.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “ate bread.”

The Hebrew word קְשִׂיטָה (qesitah) is generally understood to refer to a unit of money, but the value is unknown.sn The Hebrew word refers to a piece of silver, yet uncoined. It is the kind used in Gen 33:19 and Josh 24:32. It is what would be expected of a story set in the patriarchal age.
This gold ring was worn by women in the nose, or men and women in the ear.
verses.commentary:
42:11 "for all the evil that the Lord
had brought on him" Notice there is no mention of "the
accuser" of Job 1-2. Notice, too, the theological emphasis on one,
and only one, causality (i.e., no secondary causes, cf. Job 2:10; Eccl. 7:14;
Isa. 45:7; Jer. 32:42; Lam 3:33-38; Amos 3:6).

▣ "one piece of money"
This name of the amount is "gesitah" (BDB 903, KB
1150), which comes from an Arabic root, "to divide," and
referred to a weight of something valuable. It occurs only in an early
period (cf. Gen. 33:19; Josh. 24:32) and here.

verses.zh: 这样，耶和华后来赐福给约伯比先前更多。他有一万四千羊，六千骆驼，一千对牛，一千母驴。
verses.en: So the Lord blessed the second part of Job’s life more than the first. He had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

verses.zh: 他也有七个儿子，三个女儿。
verses.en: And he also had seven sons[NOTE:1] and three daughters.
notes: The word for “seven” is spelled in an unusual way. From this some have thought it means “twice seven,” or fourteen sons. Several commentators take this view, but it is probably not warranted.
verses.commentary:
42:13 As far as we know, Job had only one wife! Oh my!

▣ "sons. . .daughters"
One of my problems with the historicity of the book is the death of the
sons, daughters, and servants in Job 1-2. These were unique persons made
in God's image and likeness. Just to restore a given number does not
reduce the pain I feel! I know I am a North American who has grown up in
a culture that glorifies the individual, but still, I think every
individual is precious to God. For me, Job is a literary production by a
Judean sage using a past, famous person who suffered terrible tragedy!

Note that Job has the same number of "sons" and "daughters"
as before (cf. Job 1:2).

verses.zh: 他给长女起名叫耶米玛，次女叫基洗亚，三女叫基连・哈朴。
verses.en: The first daughter he named Jemimah,[NOTE:1] the second Keziah,[NOTE:2] and the third Keren-Happuch.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew name Jemimah means “dove.”
The Hebrew name Keziah means “cassia.”
The Hebrew name Keren-Happuch means “horn of eye-paint.”
verses.commentary:
42:14 The naming of daughters is
unusual in the ANE, especially when the sons are not named.

verses.zh: 在那全地的妇女中找不着像约伯的女儿那样美貌。她们的父亲使她们在弟兄中得产业。
verses.en: Nowhere in all the land could women be found who were as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and their father granted them an inheritance alongside their brothers.
verses.commentary:
42:15 It was also unusual for
daughters to inherit in the ANE (cf. Numbers 27).

verses.zh: 此后，约伯又活了一百四十年，得见他的儿孙，直到四代。
verses.en: After this Job lived 140 years; he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
verses.commentary:
42:16 The age of Job (i.e., 140 years) is another hint of the
historical setting of the book (i.e., second millennium B.C.).

verses.zh: 这样，约伯年纪老迈，日子满足而死。
verses.en: And so Job died, old and full of days.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Job 42:1-6 is Job's second response to YHWH. If his answer was
not adequate the first time (i.e., Job 40:3-5), his second response
clearly shows spiritual insight has come. He is not just silent, he is
overwhelmed!

- The book of Job is characterized by dialogues and responses. The
pattern holds throughout the book (except for Elihu's speeches).

Worldviews and traditional wisdom are conveyed
in this literary structure.

- One would expect a clear conclusion to the issue of

- innocent suffering

- the modification of "the two ways"

- where "true" wisdom is found

but in vain, one looks for answers to these questions (see Introduction
to Job, IX and Contextual Insights to Job 38, A and B). The conclusion is surprising.

- Job is affirmed (i.e., Job 42:9), even though he has attacked
the character and justice of God/YHWH.

- The three comforters, whose theology is certainly as good as
Job's, are condemned (i.e., Job 42:7-9).

- Elihu and his speeches are ignored. Why, is uncertain.

- "The two ways" is affirmed by God's actions of estoring
Job's family and fortune (i.e., Job 42:10-17).

- The accuser (i.e., Satan of chapters 1 and 2) is not mentioned at all!
